diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that matrices $B_{1},\dotsc,B_{d}\in\R^{b\times b}$ have disjoint real spectra contained in $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The ratios defining $\chim(B_k;\calB_{-k})$ divide by $\|\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}I-\Lambda_i^{(k)}\|$ and $\|\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}I-\Lambda_i^{(k)}\|$. If a block $\Lambda_i$ is a scalar matrix equal to a cluster endpoint (e.g., an extremal eigenvalue of multiplicity $b$, as occurs for multiple eigenvalues), the denominator vanishes; the numerator then vanishes as well ($\widehat B_i$ is similar to $\Lambda_i$, hence the same scalar matrix), so the ratio is $0/0$ and the maximum defining $\chim$, hence $\chim\chic$, is undefined. The interval endpoints are naturally the extremal eigenvalues and are attained, and no hypothesis excludes this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt the convention that a ratio whose denominator vanishes is 0 (consistent, because $\|\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}I-\Lambda_i\|=0$ forces $\Lambda_i=\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}I$ and then $\widehat B_i=\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}I$, so the numerator vanishes too), or restrict the maximum to indices with nonzero denominator; the growth-bound derivation is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: $\chim$ and $\chic$ (eq:defchi) are undefined for such spectra; the growth estimate eq:Gd in thm:interpolation, the estimate $G_d\le(\chim\chic/\gap)^{d-1}$ used in the conjecture section, conj:chi, and the derivation of conj:sb are all ill-defined in this case.
issues.title: Definition of chim divides by zero when a block is scalar at a cluster endpoint
issues.why_classification: A one-line convention restores well-definedness with no change to any argument, bound, or downstream result; the method and advertised conclusions survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Phi\in\poly_{d-1}(\R^{b\times b})$ be a lambda-matrix. Suppose that matrices $B_{1},\dotsc,B_{d}\in\R^{b\times b}$ have disjoint real spectra contained in $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: For $d=1$ the exponent $1/(d-1)$ is undefined and the minimum ranges over the empty set of pairs $1\le i\ne j\le1$, so eq:Gd is meaningless as stated; thm:interpolation imposes no $d\ge2$ hypothesis. The interpolation formula itself remains valid for $d=1$ (where $\fp[B_1;\calB_{-1}]=I$), and the applications use $d\ge2$ or the quantity $G_d$ directly, so only the displayed bound is affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State eq:Gd under the hypothesis $d\ge2$ (the $d=1$ case is trivial: $\max_k\|\fp[B_k;\calB_{-k}](\lambda)\|=1$).
issues.overall_effect: eq:Gd, part of thm:interpolation, is undefined for $d=1$; the conjecture-section estimate $G_d\le(\chim\chic/\gap)^{d-1}$, which quotes eq:Gd, inherits the restriction.
issues.title: Growth bound eq:Gd is meaningless for d=1
issues.why_classification: Adding the hypothesis $d\ge2$ is a standard local condition; every application uses $d\ge2$ or avoids eq:Gd, so nothing substantive is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem only assumes that $m=n/b$ is an integer, which permits $m=d$ (i.e., $n=bd$ and $\Lambda_\perp$ empty). Then the index sets $d+1\le j\le m$ in $c_\Omega$ are empty and $\log(2(m-d)/\delta)=\log 0$ is undefined, so the second assertion of thm:sb is meaningless; the main bound is vacuous in this case ($\sqrt{dn-bd^2}=0$ and $\tan\angle=0$).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $m>d$ (equivalently $\Lambda_\perp\ne\emptyset$) to thm:sb; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability bound on $c_\Omega$ in thm:sb is undefined at the boundary case $m=d$; the structural bound eq:mainsb is unaffected (it holds trivially).
issues.title: thm:sb's probabilistic assertion is ill-defined when m=d
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition fixes the degenerate case; the main result and its proof are untouched and the case $m=d$ is trivial anyway.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For any column full-rank matrix $C\in\R^{bd\times b}$ with the partition $C^{\Ttran}=[C_{0}^{\Ttran},\dotsc,C_{d-1}^{\Ttran}]$, where $C_{i}\in\R^{b\times b}$, we define a matrix polynomial $\Phi\in\poly_{d-1}(\R^{b\times b})$ as 
\Phi(X) = C_{0}+XC_{1}+\dotsb+X^{d-1}C_{d-1} \quad \forall\,X\in\R^{b\times b}.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\Phi(X)=C_0+XC_1+\dots+X^{d-1}C_{d-1}$ and $C=[C_0;\dots;C_{d-1}]$, the $k$th block row of $\van C$ is $\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}B_k^iC_i=\Phi(B_k)$, so $\van C=[\Phi(B_1);\dots;\Phi(B_d)]$, not the transposed stack claimed; the two stacks have different spectral norms in general (e.g., $A_1=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$, $A_2=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix}$ give $\|[A_1;A_2]\|=\sqrt2$ but $\|[A_1^{\Ttran};A_2^{\Ttran}]\|=1$). Hence the derivation of the key estimate eq:pfthmmain3 rests on a false identity. The same spurious transpose appears in the bound displayed in thm:interpolation, but that displayed inequality is nevertheless true (apply $\sum_k\|M_kx\|^2\le d\|[M_1;\dots;M_d]\|^2\|x\|^2$ with $M_k=\Phi(B_k)^{\Ttran}$). With the corrected identity, the proof of eq:mainsb goes through unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $[\Phi^{\Ttran}(B_{1}),\dotsc,\Phi^{\Ttran}(B_{d})]^{\Ttran}$ by $[\Phi(B_{1}),\dotsc,\Phi(B_{d})]^{\Ttran}$ in the proof of thm:sb; the transposed display in thm:interpolation may be kept (it is valid) or aligned with the corrected identity.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:sb is invalid as written at the reduction to matrix polynomials; the main bound eq:mainsb remains correct, since the forced correction (remove the transposes) yields a valid proof of the same conclusion, and no dependent result is affected.
issues.title: Proof of thm:sb uses the false identity van*C = [Phi^T(B_k)]^T
issues.why_classification: The false identity has a single forced correction visible directly from the definition of $\Phi$, and after the correction the whole proof and every conclusion survive; the repair is local and routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since all $\Omega_{i}$ and $\Omega_{j}$ are $b\times b$ Gaussian random matrices for $1\leq i\leq d<j\leq m$, the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing $c_\Omega=\sqrt{dn-bd^2}\,M_1M_2M_3$ with $M_1=\max_{i\le d}\|\Omega_i^{-1}\|$, $M_2=\max_{j>d}\|\Omega_j\|$, $M_3=\max_{j>d}\|\Omega_j\|\|\Omega_j^{-1}\|$, the stated tail bounds plus union bounds give, with failure probability at most $(m+1)\delta$ (not $4\delta$), $M_1\le\sqrt b/\delta$, $M_2\le L$, $M_3\le L\sqrt b/\delta$ with $L=2\sqrt b+\sqrt{2\log(2(m-d)/\delta)}$, hence $c_\Omega^2\le(dn-bd^2)\,b^2\,\delta^{-4}L^4$. The claimed $(dn-bd^2)^3\delta^{-4}L$ would require $b^2L^3\le(dn-bd^2)^2$, i.e., $L^3\le d^2(m-d)^2$, which fails in general (e.g., $b=1$, $d=2$, $m=3$, $\delta=0.1$). So the asserted inequality is not a consequence of the paper's own ingredients and is false in general; the probability accounting $1-4\delta$ is likewise inconsistent with the union bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the union bound: with probability at least $1-(m+1)\delta$ (after relabelling $\delta$), $c_\Omega^2\le(dn-bd^2)\,b^2\,\delta^{-4}\bigl(2\sqrt b+\sqrt{2\log(2(m-d)/\delta)}\bigr)^4$; this is a contained correction giving a recognizably comparable polynomial-in-$(dn-bd^2)$, $\delta^{-4}$, logarithmic-in-$(m/\delta)$ bound, and it suffices for all downstream applications.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative high-probability bound on $c_\Omega$ in thm:sb is unreliable; the structural bound eq:mainsb is unaffected. conj:sb, cor:eig and cor:lr invoke only the abstract constant $c_{b,d,n}$, so their formal statements survive, but any quantitative use of the stated bound is wrong.
issues.title: The high-probability bound on c_Omega^2 in thm:sb does not follow from the stated tail bounds
issues.why_classification: The stated quantitative guarantee is false and must be replaced by a recomputed bound; the repair is a contained reoptimization of the probability allocation with no new proof architecture and no major loss (the corrected bound is comparable and sharper in the dominant factor $dn-bd^2$), which fits moderate rather than minor.
